messages:
maya: alerting — pool-delta nodes showing creeping memory in kv-cache, p99 bursts and a few container restarts in last 12m :warning:
inc-bot: INCIDENT OPENED #INC-2026-089 (kv-cache-slow-drip) — alert: inference.node.oom on pool-delta. severity: high. affected tenants: 2 (prod); routing degraded.
maya: symptoms: repeated CUDA allocation failures, containers restarting on nodes d-03,d-05,d-08. probing graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-cache-pool-delta
oliver: pulling logs from d-05 — allocator hitting high fragmentation and pinned refs. snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T04:01:12Z] paged_allocator.cc:502 find_run: cannot allocate contiguous pages, frag_ratio=0.81
[2026-03-15T04:01:12Z] kv_cache.cpp:312 release_page: WARN pinned_ref_count=4
[2026-03-15T04:01:12Z] cuda: failed to allocate 900MB, OOM
```
sasha: agree with maya — resident size for kv-cache steadily rising ~150MB/hr over 8h. looks like pinned pages not being released, leading to fragmentation and eventually CUDA OOMs.
maya: customer impact: CS seeing elevated errors for two customers in us-east. @aaron-cs can you confirm severity and whether fallbacks are in use?
aaron-cs: confirmed. Customer X (payments) seeing 12% errors since 03:40 UTC; Customer Y (recommendations) reporting tail latency regressions. Both on Dedicated pools. CS has routed traffic to fallback models where possible.
jordan: taking lead for runtime triage. suggested immediate mitigations:
- flip kv aggressive eviction (evict_ratio=0.15)
- lower service batch size to 1 for pool-delta
- temporarily disable paging for the handful of largest models
- cordon highest-error nodes and migrate workloads
maya: agree — prefer config flips first to reduce churn. oliver, can you apply eviction toggle? sasha will capture heap dump on d-08.
oliver: applying eviction flag to pool-delta now:
```
redctl apply --cluster pool-delta --kv-evict-ratio=0.15
```
oliver: flag active, monitoring memory.
sasha: running heap dump on d-08:
```
ssh infra@d-08 
sudo /opt/tools/kv-dump --pid $(pgrep kv-cache) --out /tmp/kv_heap_d08.tar.gz
```
sasha: uploaded dump to /artifacts/kv_d08_heap.tar.gz and shared.
inc-bot: AUTO ACTION: fallback routing enabled for pool-delta while error_rate > 4% — smaller/quantized variants will receive traffic.
jordan: after eviction + fallback, overall p50 ok but p99 still elevated for long-context requests. need to remediate nodes. planning to cordon d-03 then drain and replace.
maya: initiating targeted runtime compaction on d-05 before draining. oliver, execute compaction run.
oliver: running runtime compaction: 
```
red-runner --node d-05 --cmd="kv-allocator --compact --aggressive"
```
oliver: compaction freed ~1.2GB, fragmentation dropped to ~0.68, but pinned refs still visible.
sasha: heap analysis shows a class of pinned pages tied to older session tokens — likely a race in cleanup when request cancels mid-paging. I'll start a small repro in staging.
jordan: create repro and see if lowering in-flight concurrency forces release path. maya, set test namespace `drip-repro` to concurrency=2 and replay a mixed-length workload.
maya: done — running replay now.
aaron-cs: customers kept on fallback; will send updated status and ETA. collecting request ids for RCA logs.
jordan: next steps:
1) keep eviction toggles + batch_size=1 for 45m
2) cordon and rotate d-03,d-05,d-08 sequentially (one at a time)
3) if leak persists after node rotation, eng-runtime to cut hotfix addressing page_release fence/race
4) eng-infra to verify CUDA driver versions and kernel patches on affected hardware
5) eng-ml to look for model runtime patterns that exacerbate paging (large kv footprints)
maya: eng-ml and eng-infra looped in: @eng-ml @eng-infra. oliver starting replacement creation for d-03 -> d-19.
oliver: node replacement started: d-03 -> d-19. inc-bot notified.
inc-bot: NODE REPLACEMENT IN PROGRESS - d-03 -> d-19
maya: monitoring — after compaction + eviction + rotation of d-03, error rate dropped 12% -> 5%, p99 for long jobs reduced from 14s -> 7s. still tracking slow climb on d-08. keeping d-08 cordoned.
sasha: preparing PR with a deterministic fix and a stress test harness reproducer. PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/kv/merge_requests/3301 — includes extra atomic ops around page_release and a unit test.
jordan: eng-runtime to prioritize PR review and canary; eng-ml to validate no perf regression. eng-infra to collect kernel/cuda debug logs and confirm driver consistency across pool-delta nodes.
maya: handoff summary for next oncall shift below. leaving at 05:20 UTC.
maya: HANDOFF SUMMARY:
- root cause hypothesis: pinned KV pages not released due to a race in page_release path + fragmentation, leading to gradual memory creep and CUDA OOMs
- impact: 2 paying customers with increased 5xxs and elevated p99; traffic routed to fallback smaller models
- mitigations applied: aggressive eviction (evict_ratio=0.15), batch_size set to 1 on pool-delta, runtime bitmap compaction, node rotations (d-03 replaced), fallback routing enabled automatically above threshold
- remaining work: rotate/replace d-05,d-08; if leak persists deploy page_release hotfix PR #3301; infra to audit drivers; ml to check model-side kv patterns
- owners: jordan (lead), oliver (runtime ops), sasha (heap/debug + PR), aaron-cs (customer comms)
maya: leaving notes in incident ticket and will follow up on PR progress. :white_check_mark:
jordan: ack, taking over until 07:00 UTC. will post incident RCA when root cause validated.
aaron-cs: sending customer update now with mitigation details and ETA for full remediation.
inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED #INC-2026-089 — status: mitigated (partial). followups created: ENG-3301 (hotfix), INF-546 (driver audit), ML-223 (model memory patterns).
